items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: I started doing all of Pat’s shows, with Tony Randall and Mary Tyler Moore and Rhoda

ctx.x: Different, but you see New York was already in a state of flux at that point. It was — studios were closing down left and right in favor of synthesizers, and everything was moving toward motion pictures and T.V. And Patrick Williams had called me up and said look, because I was looking for an excuse to go out there, because I had just met Mary Ann. I took a tour and I played Donte’s out there in Los Angeles and I met this gorgeous creature, and I threw away my black book and I said this is it, this I’ve gotta…

when I called him and I got an affirmative response from him that was all the excuse I needed to go out, because I immediately went out there and I started working for Mary Ann Kline, the Klines, and I started doing all of Pat’s shows, with Tony Randall and Mary Tyler Moore and Rhoda and the Lou Grant Show and Charlie’s Angels. All these, oh and Fantasy Island. So I had all of those shows I was doing each week. This was before they went and had the strike and then they of course changed the law, the rules of the…
Why did the union do what sounds like a pretty stupid thing to do?
